s1.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The patient is a 32-year-old woman
The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
There are widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs are sparse and less than 5 mm long
Scalp hairs are coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

shortlist.label: Netherton syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic hair shaft abnormalities and ichthyosiform dermatitis

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Widespread erythematous plaques with double-edged scale

shortlist.label: Ichthyosis linearis circumflexa
shortlist.why_kept: Polycyclic serpiginous plaques with involvement of 90% BSA

shortlist.label: Atopic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive worsening and involvement of large body surface area

shortlist.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy

raw.rationale: The combination of skin findings, including erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, and hair abnormalities such as sparse eyebrow hairs and coarse brittle scalp hairs, along with the specific trichography findings of nodal swelling and invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end, are characteristic of Netherton syndrome.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: While it can present with erythematous plaques, the specific hair findings and trichography results are more indicative of Netherton syndrome.

rejected.label: Ichthyosis linearis circumflexa
rejected.why: This condition is often associated with Netherton syndrome but on its own does not account for the full spectrum of the patient's symptoms, particularly the hair findings.

rejected.label: Atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: The presence of psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy and the specific pattern of hair involvement are not typical for atopic dermatitis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, the clinical presentation and particularly the hair findings are not characteristic of psoriasis vulgaris.
